The engineering reality behind behind the meter power starts from the physical constraint that a 100 megawatts cluster already matches the output of a small gas turbine and every GPU rack pulls tens of kilowatts without interruption.

At several hundred megawatts, the cooling plant grows comparable in scale and complexity to the generation equipment.

The resulting setup accepts higher upfront capital in exchange for reduced variable electricity cost and quicker permitting compared with waiting for utility scale transmission upgrades.

The recent hosting contract supplies one such anchor load that can cover fixed plant costs while remaining capacity scales.
